analysisSummary: Independently reproduced with a minimal fixture: the new @role: check prints DRIFT yet the script exits 0 and reports CLEAN. The enforcement gate (pre-commit hook + CI) silently passes on the exact drift class it was added to catch; CHANGELOG's 'Red-tested' claim could only have asserted stdout.
suggestedFix: Hoist the loop out of the pipeline (read into an array first, or use process substitution / lastpipe), make the trailing ok() conditional on the collected failures.

analysisSummary: Re-ran roleBody on the real agents/worker.md: the dispatch-note HTML comment survives into the substituted prompt. The code's own inline comment states the note should be dropped; the regex assumes comment-before-Role order, real files are Role-then-comment. Orchestrator-facing meta-instructions leak into every @role: subagent prompt.
suggestedFix: Strip the comment regardless of position relative to the Role header (e.g. remove the leading # Role: line first, then the leading comment), and add a test asserting the comment is gone for the real file layout.

analysisSummary: Verified all four '<verbatim body>' templates in prompts/next.md against the three normative docs mandating @role:. Two normative sources specify different shapes for the same default dispatch, and next.md (the most-used entry point) never points at dispatch-shapes.md. Behavioral consequence: nondeterministic orchestration style and the extension's substitution path may never fire for /next sessions following the inline template.
suggestedFix: Update next.md's four templates to prompt: '@role:<name>' with the fallback note, and reference agents/dispatch-shapes.md.

analysisSummary: Direct file read confirms duplicate '4.' step numbering introduced by the inserted README-freshness step.
bun test: 25 tests; CHANGELOG claims 13. Verifiable factual error in the shipped changelog.
suggestedFix: Correct the count (or drop the number to avoid future drift).

analysisSummary: File-count vs task-count masking is real and reachable after an abandoned plan, but the watchdog is explicitly reminder-grade and the normal flow (per-task files, SHIP archiving) limits the window. Whether to tighten (match review files to done task ids) is a design decision.
suggestedFix: Derive finalOkTrue per done task id (reviews/<task-id>.md containing a final '**ok: true**') rather than a global file count.

analysisSummary: Both behaviors verified in source (changelogPending ignores CHANGELOG.md content; dedupe is boolean-episode, not gap-count as the header/CHANGELOG claim). Each is defensible as reminder-grade; the internal doc contradiction (header vs inline comment) should be resolved by a human choosing the intended contract.
suggestedFix: Pick one dedupe contract and align header comment + CHANGELOG; optionally read CHANGELOG.md to clear changelogPending after the SHIP entry exists.
